upcoming.expectation: First update to the survey-based yields — September asks whether August's 180.7 corn / 52.7 soybean numbers hold after a hot mid-August finish.

biggest_surprise.reaction: USDA's first survey-based corn yield came in at 180.7 — 2.3 under July and 1.3 under the trade's 182.0. More acres (planted up 1.4M to 96.7M) kept production near-record at 16.013B bu, but the market traded the yield cut and the 1.653B carryout (down from 1.79B): December corn settled up 15 cents at $4.78.

history.reaction: USDA's first survey-based corn yield came in at 180.7 — 2.3 under July and 1.3 under the trade's 182.0. More acres (planted up 1.4M to 96.7M) kept production near-record at 16.013B bu, but the market traded the yield cut and the 1.653B carryout (down from 1.79B): December corn settled up 15 cents at $4.78.

Soybean yield printed 52.7 — a couple tenths under both July and the trade, effectively in line. The acreage add (planted up 1.4M to 86.8M) still makes 4.519B bu the largest soybean crop on record, and carryout ticked up to 320M. November beans settled up 12 cents at $11.84, riding corn's coattails more than their own numbers.

The report's one real surprise: new-crop wheat carryout cut to 744M — 21M below the trade and 18M under May — on a smaller Hard Red Winter crop (all-wheat production trimmed to 1,543M, yield 47.0). Bullish wheat; farm price cut $0.50 to $6.00.
Old-crop carryout landed right on the trade guess — a non-event for corn.
New-crop carryout nudged up fractionally on old-crop demand tweaks; essentially unchanged at $4.40.
Old-crop beans unchanged from May and on top of the trade — no reaction.
New-crop beans held at 310, a hair under the trade — quietly friendly but no fireworks.
Old-crop wheat held at 935, just under the trade guess.
